newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranian minister opposes amending constitution.
newsitem.headline: Iranian minister opposes amending constitution.

text.p: Iran's Interior Minister Ali Mohammad Besharati said on Sunday it was not in Iran's interest to change the constitution to allow the re-election of President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani for a third term.
The official news agency IRNA said Besharati told reporters that "unlike some countries we should not amend the constitution and expose it to the aspirations of certain political groups".
"The issue of the constitution amendment should no longer be raised especially by the press," he added.
A leading Iranian parliamentarian last month called for the removal of legal barriers blocking the re-election of Rafsanjani, a view reiterated by some of the Iranian media.
Rafsanjani's second term ends in July 1997. The constitution bars three consecutive terms and Rafsanjani has repeatedly stressed his unwillingness to seek a third term by changing the constitution.
